claims.claim: Recycled PET commands roughly $1,300-1,700 per metric ton in the US market (Q2 2026 US average about USD 1,389/MT), within the digest's $1,300-2,600/t range for cleaned, pelletized material.
claims.episode_span: PET and HDPE at roughly $1,300–2,600 per ton once cleaned and pelletized
claims.source_title: R-PET Price Trend and Forecast - ChemAnalyst
claims.supporting_quote: In USA, the R-PET Price Index fell by 11.49% quarter-over-quarter, reflecting converter procurement and inventory accumulation. The average R-PET price for the quarter was approximately USD 1388.67/MT

claims.episode_span: clear glass cullet at about forty dollars per ton

claims.claim: Single-stream recycling spread widely across US municipalities after its early-1990s introduction; by 2013, 100 million Americans were served by single-stream programs.
claims.episode_span: Single-stream collection, adopted widely in North America after 2000, lets households place all recyclables in one bin.
claims.supporting_quote: As of 2012, there are 248 MRFs operating in the US. [ 12 ] As of 2013, 100 million Americans were served by single-stream programs

claims.claim: Single-stream collection increases contamination in the recycling stream and can reduce the commodity prices of the recovered materials.
claims.episode_span: That convenience raised participation rates but delivered a heavily contaminated stream
claims.supporting_quote: Increase of contamination in the recycling container. Possible reduced commodity prices due to contamination of paper or plastic

claims.claim: Sorting single-stream material is expensive relative to output value: a 2020 industry survey found single-stream MRF processing costs of $112 per ton versus $60 for dual-stream/source-separated facilities, with costs rising each survey.
claims.episode_span: Each additional handling step adds direct wages plus the carrying cost of slower throughput.
claims.source_title: Survey shows fast-rising MRF processing costs - Resource Recycling
claims.supporting_quote: the survey found much higher processing costs for single-stream facilities ($112 per ton) compared with dual-stream and source-separated ones ($60 per ton)
